changes.reason: Move the frozen edge out of the entangled low conduction bands (where it causes subspace kinks and long-range tails) to just below the top of the nearly isolated 8-band sp3 manifold; validate_deck gives at most 8 energy-frozen states for 8 functions.

diagnosis: The untruncated model is accurate (4.32 meV), with centres on atoms and balanced spreads (ratio 1.24). The truncated model fails (30.9 meV) because the Hamiltonian decays slowly (tau ≈ 2.0 Å) for sp3 functions in a gapped crystal. The cause is a non-smooth disentangled subspace: the frozen edge at 3.92 eV cuts through the entangled conduction bands 5–7. States frozen on the mesh at 3.3–3.8 eV are interpolated 0.4–1.0 eV off along the path, a kink signature, and band 5 near (0, ½, ½) at 1.7–1.9 eV is 60 meV off untruncated and about 200 meV off truncated. The truncated error is 14 meV with valence only and jumps to 31 meV once those conduction states enter the E_F+2 window. Bands 1–8 form a nearly isolated manifold (top 14.573 eV, band 9 from 14.553 eV), so freezing almost all of it removes the kink from the measured range. The result should be a smooth subspace and faster-decaying hoppings. The frontier retry ladder only varies the projectability thresholds, which leaves the energy edge in place; the corpus held no matching repair.
